notes.1: The great majority of candidates gained full marks. Those that did not usually chose ink jet instead of dot matrix printer.
notes.2: Almost all candidates gained both marks.
notes.3: The vast majority of candidates gained full marks. A small number, however, thought that PDAs could not be used unless plugged in to an electricity socket.
notes.4: Candidates did quite well on this question with many gaining full marks. Incorrect answers were spread evenly amongst the different statements.
notes.5: The vast majority of candidates scored well. A small number gave queries as an answer instead of ‘whatifs’.
notes.6: Most candidates were able to name the instructions but descriptions of the instructions were sometimes not in sufficient detail. PENUP and PENDOWN seemed to cause the candidates most issues when it came to defining them. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0417 Information Technology June 2011
notes.7: Candidates gave many incorrect answers for this question including ‘it is more private to send a fax’.
notes.8: The candidates need a further understanding the concept of real time processing. Many answers given did not contain sufficient detail.
notes.10: This question was quite well answered. Most candidates were able to name at least two appropriate checks.
notes.11: This question was answered very well.
notes.12: Candidates frequently provided answers which were general security techniques rather than authentication techniques. Many candidates answered with encryption and firewalls. A number of candidates did not mention usernames and passwords together.
notes.13: Candidates did very well on this question. (a) The vast majority of candidates were able to provide correct answers. (b) A number of candidates had rote-learnt previous mark and gave answers which were methods of preventing health problems. Others continued on from part (a) and gave another two health problems. The majority of candidates were able to gain both marks.
notes.14: This question produced a mixed set of responses with virtually all candidates able to gain at least one mark. Many candidates gave business type answers rather than answers that referred to schools. Candidates answered the advantages part better than the disadvantages part.
notes.15: Many of the candidates failed to pick up on the requirement for navigation aids and instead gave answers relating to features of the screen such as font size, filling the page etc. a number of candidates gave the names of fields that would be found in the database. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0417 Information Technology June 2011
notes.16: Most candidates performed better on part (a) than they did on (b) (a) Many candidates knew the names of the methods. Candidates found it difficult to give an advantage, preferring instead to describe the method, and many could not provide a disadvantage. A sizeable number of advantages of the first method were then given as disadvantages of the second method and vice versa, thereby limiting the number of marks available. (b) Candidates did not appear to know how evaluation is carried out. Many referred to other aspects of systems analysis instead.
notes.17: Many candidates gained just one mark for the laziness aspect. A sizeable number of candidates tended to write about the devices but did not relate these to the effects on lifestyles i.e. how we lead our lives. High performing candidates scored very well.
notes.18: Overall, this question was very well answered in parts (a) and (b) but then poorly answered in part (c) . (a) The vast majority of candidates gained full marks. (b) Most candidates gained full marks. (c) Candidates need to mention the microprocessor or what function it performs. Many candidates incorrectly stated that the sensors controlled the process.
notes.19: Most candidates managed to gain at least one mark with the higher ability candidates gaining 3 or 4 marks. Most candidates who scored well concentrated on phishing and pharming.
notes.20: This question was better answered with the majority of candidates gaining at least two marks. Most gained marks for portability and having a smaller display but did not mention other mark scheme points. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0417 Information Technology June 2011 INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
notes.9a: A number of candidates had leant previous mark schemes by rote to a differently phrased question, that of creating an expert system. This meant that these candidates found it difficult to gain any marks.
notes.9b: Most candidates were able to name at least one other use.
